scope: Source-only independent review; no native or heavy test run

currentSource.driftFromSnapshot: Current use-network-capture.ts additionally clears partial events and source on discovery failure; findings below apply to both snapshot and current source.

verdictA.reason: No installed development extension, real HN Search initial request, saved-row persistence, reopened Patterns, or two native replays were exercised in this source lane.

positiveEvidence: Discovery enters the SW-owned Port and requestConfirmation with the cdp_attach privileged admin/debugger policy; executePreparedOperation rechecks tab URL and document identity before capture (document-network-transport.ts:110-175; dispatch.ts:1673-1691,1783-1896).

The document capture core whitelists event fields, omits request headers and raw request bodies, pins capture/document identity, and closes its CDP lease (document-network-capture.ts:107-175,195-207,330-377). Saved replay still compares request_body_key exactly (run-interactive.ts:394-412).

findings.title: Captured page and persisted recipe route can diverge during a same-tab navigation
findings.evidence: use-network-capture.ts:102-120 takes sourceFromUrl(tab.url) from the asynchronous useActiveTab React state, but dispatch.ts:1803-1821 independently reads the live tab URL/document and approves that page. The discovery Port returns only events/progress/result (document-network-transport.ts:179-219), so the hook never reconciles the approved URL. NetworkTab.tsx:360-375 passes the cached source into SaveAsPattern, which persists its host and route at SaveAsPattern.tsx:85-90,154-165. If onUpdated has fired but its async refresh has not committed, discovery can succeed for the new same-tab page while Save writes the old route. The event URL alone does not establish the top-frame route.
findings.requiredFix: Return the SW-approved top-frame page URL with the discovery result or a bound start message, and derive the save source from that identity. Add a navigation-race test that proves the persisted recipe host/route matches the captured document.

findings.title: New connected discovery test cannot prove initial-document delivery
findings.evidence: document-network-dispatch.test.ts:98-108 mocks openDocumentNetworkCapture to call onArmed and onEvent with the expected event. Its fixture lacks request_sequence, which the real document-network-capture.ts:330-345 rejects as incomplete. document-network-port.test.ts:96-128 also mocks the entire discovery runner and supplies its own event. Existing document-network-capture.test.ts:175-224 proves core buffering separately, but no new test carries an approved operation through the real capture core and Port into the picker. A broken connection between approval and document-start capture can leave these new tests green.
findings.requiredFix: Use the real discovery dispatcher, Port and document capture core with Chrome/CDP APIs stubbed below them. Feed an initial-document event with request_sequence and a distinct body digest; assert the exact event reaches the selection/save seam, then prove a wrong-document or wrong-body event cannot satisfy it.

findings.title: Zero-response completion gives a misleading selection instruction
findings.evidence: runLocalNetworkDiscovery resolves { ok: true } when its 20-second window ends without any event (dispatch.ts:1843-1870), then use-network-capture.ts:121 unconditionally says 'Select a response below.' NetworkTab.tsx:185-188 instead presents the generic manual-capture instruction when the event list is empty.
findings.requiredFix: Report a truthful empty page-load result with a retry or page-interaction remedy.
